A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpiLiFormer research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, attention-module ablations, adversarial evaluations, and attention visualizations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds loss-weight sensitivity results and inference-latency measurements in Appendix A.4–A.5.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the same neuron dynamics, FF-LiDiff and two-pass FB-LiDiff procedures, architecture, and weighted loss. The default α = 0.5 already appears in v1; its new ablation does not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five classification datasets, CIFAR-10-C and ImageNet-1K-C corruption scenarios, and FGSM/PGD attacks. The added sensitivity and latency experiments use existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–2 and the adversarial comparisons. The new latency analysis reuses the already defined variant without FB-LiDiff rather than introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 adds an α sweep over 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, and 0.7, plus per-sample latency comparisons with and without FB-LiDiff. Existing training schedules, model configurations, time steps, resolutions, and attack settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.4 tests sensitivity to the loss-mixing weight on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR10-DVS. Appendix A.5 measures the computational overhead of feedback across five datasets. These targeted analyses supplement the retained module ablations and robustness tests.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new appendix tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: The original benchmark, module-ablation, and adversarial values are unchanged. New Table 4 adds nondefault α results, including 96.16% CIFAR-10 accuracy at α = 0.7. Table 5 newly reports feedback latency increases of 1.2%–23.2% across the five datasets.

T1.justification: Equations 1–27 retain the same neuron dynamics, attention computations, loss, adversarial updates, and energy-estimation formulas. No substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: lateral-inhibition attention, state-of-the-art classification on five datasets, and improved attention allocation and robustness. The added analyses support existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 adds an explicit accuracy–latency tradeoff, attributing additional delay to FB-LiDiff's second forward pass and acknowledging roughly 21–23% overhead on static CIFAR datasets. Appendix A.4 also interprets the new sweep as supporting α = 0.5 among the tested values.

D1.justification: v1 promises code and training checkpoints upon acceptance. v2 supplies a repository link and reports code and model checkpoints as publicly available. Existing implementation details remain unchanged; the new latency evaluation does not specify timing hardware or measurement procedures.

R1.justification: The same 49 references and related-work discussions are retained. Positioning relative to existing spiking Transformers and lateral-inhibition research is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized additions to Sections 3.5 and 4.5, introduces two appendix subsections and acknowledgments, shortens the contact information, and makes small wording corrections. The main narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is refreshed with sharper images and revised mathematical labels and legend. Two compact appendix tables are added; the original adversarial Table 4 becomes Table 6. Existing figures are retained, with limited table-spacing and page-layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens validation of the existing loss weight and makes the feedback latency cost explicit, improving the balance of the discussion. Reported code and checkpoint access also improves reproducibility information. These are useful, limited gains: the central results remain unchanged, and the added measurements lack uncertainty reporting and a reproducible timing protocol.
